request: I want a housing for an Arduino Uno R3 board — 68.6 x 53.3 mm with four 3.2 mm mounting holes — which rests on four standoffs located at the board's mounting holes. The board has a USB-B port and a 5.5 mm barrel jack along the same short edge, and I need to be able to plug both in while the cover is on and the cables are attached, meaning the moulded handle of each plug as well as the metal has to pass through the wall. Cut a line of ventilation slots into the cover above the ATmega328P, and fix the cover down with four M3 self-tapping screws. It's a base and a detachable cover, printed in PLA on an FDM machine with no supports, and I must be able to take the board out for servicing. Requirements: Pick the Arduino Uno R3 from the parts catalogue, state its pose, and locate its USB-B receptacle and DC jack — both on one short edge of the board — at one and the same short end of the case. With the case shut, the 68.6 x 53.3 x 1.6 mm board must have at least 0.5 mm of space to every printed surface, other than at its standoffs. Support the board on four standoffs, neither more nor fewer, one at each of its four mounting holes. Outside diameter is 5 to 7 mm, their top planes agree within 0.1 mm, and each carries a pilot hole deep enough for a 10 mm M3 self-tapping screw to seat (the 1.6 mm board counted). Case closed, nothing may be closer than 12 mm above the board's top surface or 4 mm beneath its underside; the standoffs at the holes are the only exception. Case closed, a USB-B plug, shell and moulded handle both, must go right into the receptacle through a single opening in the end wall with 0.3 mm or more between it and the case on every side, and the opening can be no more than 1.5 mm larger than the plug on any side. Case closed, a 5.5 x 2.1 mm DC barrel plug including its moulded handle must go fully into the jack via a separate opening in that same end wall while the USB plug is in as well, keeping 0.3 mm or more clear of the case all round, and the opening can exceed the plug by 1.5 mm at most on any side. Fit the lid with a straight line of 5 to 9 vent slots right above the ATmega328P. Each is 1.5 to 3.0 mm wide and 8 to 12 mm long on a 3.5 to 6.5 mm pitch, and the open area adds up to at least 100 mm². Build the case from a base and a separate lid that can be removed: the lid is a flat plate sitting in a rebate cut in the top of the walls (2 to 3 mm plate, 0.15 to 0.35 mm gap per side as fit, upstand of at least 1 mm), held by four M3 self-tapping screws that go into four bosses in the base. When closed the case has no holes except for the USB opening, the DC opening, the vent slots and the screw holes, and the walls, floor and lid are 2 to 4 mm thick. Each of base and lid is a single manifold body for FDM printing with no supports: overhangs no steeper than 45° from vertical and bridges no longer than 15 mm. Overall the closed case is limited to 100 x 70 x 35 mm, with the longest dimension along the board's 68.6 mm side, and it should sit flat on a desk without tipping over. With the lid removed, the populated board must lower straight onto the standoffs, a screwdriver must reach every board screw, and the screws for the lid must be distinct from those for the board. Deliver the base STL, the lid STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared board pose and the agent's own clearance report; the report has to agree with an independent measurement.
